name: Teal Alder
life: “My first delivery bag had a strap so long it banged my knee.” Monday often includes a stop at Juniper Street, where Teal knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I offered to deliver them and discovered that two people who worked together for years never knew each other's addresses.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a plum-colored cardigan and one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. Teal has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with short copper curls. Teal takes off the watch before a long conversation during a conversation.
personality: Teal loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Teal remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To deliver all five tins to the people who used them.
family: Iva Salas is Teal’s older cousin. Teal brings the paper and a pen. Iva decides what stays off the paper. They have helped each other make decisions that were far easier to discuss once the figures could be moved around. The decisions themselves still belong to the person asking. Asked about *The returned daughter*, Iva says, “I thought the house would look smaller. The door still feels exactly as high as the day I left.”
connections: Hamish Nichols. They help return the named tins without blaming the casual crews.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Teal asks the nearest shop worker to stay too, then talks about ordinary things until the child can explain who is late.
